A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GALAX framework and Target-QA study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite expanded experiments and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on Target-QA, component comparisons, pretraining results and biological enrichment analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds comparator evaluations, robustness experiments, held-out cancer tests, PedDep evaluation and human/LLM assessments.

M1.justification: The initial/final answering pipeline, pretrained GNN, edge-generation policy, rollout and rule rewards, acceptance gating and training objectives are retained. The schema rules emphasized in v2 already appear in v1. Qwen and reward-interval experiments evaluate variants of the existing procedure rather than introduce a new core method.

E1.justification: v2 adds external evaluation on 31 PedDep pediatric cancer cell lines and scenarios with missing omic modalities or depleted graph structure. The original Target-QA cancer coverage remains. Holding out existing cancer types changes the evaluation split rather than adding cancer categories.

E2.justification: RoG, SubgraphRAG and GNN-RAG become evaluated comparators in Tables 1–2 and the corresponding appendix cohort tables. RoG was previously cited but not evaluated. Existing comparators remain after matching expanded Omics and pre-GAT labels.

E3.justification: The original Target-QA split and metrics are retained, but v2 introduces three cancer-type holdout designs, zero-shot PedDep evaluation, a Qwen2.5-7B backbone, graph/input perturbation controls and varied reward intervals. Appendix E.2 also introduces a five-point biological-relevance assessment of ten examples by three bioinformaticians and two LLMs.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component comparisons and enrichment cases, v2 tests graph node/edge deletion, individual and complete omics removal, reward density, and removal of the graph supervisor, rules, rollouts and gating. Backbone and cancer-transfer analyses and expert/LLM plausibility assessments substantially broaden validation. The existing enrichment cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 15 newly reports individual judge scores and per-example mean ± standard deviation across human and LLM raters. The existing four-seed experimental statement and five-trial training analyses remain unchanged; additional benchmark error bars do not establish increased run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive comparator, Qwen, robustness, holdout, PedDep and rating results. Original overall GALAX precision/recall remain 0.5472/0.5332; newly reported held-out average F1 is 0.4862 and PedDep LLaMA-GALAX F1 is 0.2901 under different settings. Some existing baseline values also change: ESCA L3-FT(Med) precision rises from 0.0047 to 0.0143, while L3+KG becomes zero.

T1.justification: Section 5 extends the asymptotic complexity analysis to RoG, SubgraphRAG and GNN-RAG. It also corrects the static-KG baseline's prose cost from O(κ + M²ε) to O(κ + M²), matching Table 3. Core mathematical objectives remain unchanged, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim integration of omics, text and biological graphs through GPRM-guided subgraph construction without intermediate reasoning labels, and introduce Target-QA. v2 foregrounds existing schema rules and rephrases the conclusion without materially changing these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning transfer to unseen cancers, external generalization, missing-input robustness and immediate versus delayed rewards. Appendix D.2 newly explains four existing components as defenses against reward hacking. Appendix D.3 qualifies the added baselines' supervision as noisy and biologically incomplete, while E.2 interprets expert/LLM plausibility judgments.

D1.justification: v2 documents ChatGPT-5.1-generated training paths for the added retrieval baselines and explicitly describes the reward classifier as frozen. Existing training hyperparameters and hardware are largely unchanged. The reproducibility statement now points to supplementary source code, while GitHub and Hugging Face links remain in the abstract.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SubgraphRAG, GNN-RAG and PedDep and sharpens its positioning against methods dependent on reliable retrieved subgraphs and reasoning-path supervision. The broader related-work organization and claimed integration novelty remain intact.

P1.justification: Section 3 reorganizes its explanation into feature, textual and topological spaces and separates Target-QA input components. Introduction, related-work and conclusion passages receive localized rewrites, and appendices gain subdivisions. Most existing method, pretraining and enrichment prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated tables for perturbations, reward analyses, holdout assignments/results, PedDep, judge ratings and cancer-code definitions. Existing performance tables gain grouped comparator and Qwen rows, and Figures 4a and 11 are redrawn with additional model series. These substantially expand the visual presentation beyond renumbering or numerical edits.

improvement.justification: v2 directly tests transferability and reward-component contributions that v1 supported mainly through the standard Target-QA evaluation and enrichment examples. Additional graph baselines, held-out cancers, PedDep, targeted ablations and expert ratings substantially strengthen the empirical basis. Some interpretations overreach: reward-hacking prevention is not directly tested, and LLaMA-GALAX trails GNN-RAG on PedDep Hit@10 (0.5179 versus 0.5333). Despite these qualifications and the ten-case rating sample, the targeted validation provides a substantial net improvement.
